children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were weaker at midday Wednesday, taking back some of Tuesday's gains as chart- based positioning weighed on values.
November canola was down by C$6.20 at C$832.90 per tonne at midsession.
The losses came despite gains in crude oil, which was underpinned by the escalating tensions in the Middle East.
The Chicago soy complex was mixed at midday, with losses in beans but a firmer tone in soyoil.
Statistics Canada reported canola ending stocks as of July 31, 2026, at 1.9 million tonnes. That was up by 19 percent on the year but in line with trade estimates and the five-year average.
Recent rains across parts of Western Canada Prairies provided some underlying support, as the untimely moisture flooded some fields and raised concerns over potential harvest delays.

Statistics Canada will release its first production estimates for 2026-27 on Sept. 16. Updated U.S. supply/demand estimates from the United States Department of Agriculture will be released on Friday, Sept. 11.
An estimated 33,700 canola contracts traded as of 11:48 EDT.
